head.h1: BBQ Catering in Dubai — Menus, Prices and What's Included

opening_paragraph: BBQ catering in Dubai from myCHEF is priced from AED 700 per person , and it brings a live grill and a working chef to your venue. Garden, villa, rooftop or beach — the fire goes where you are. The smoke, the char and the timing all happen in front of your guests instead of in a back kitchen. One team handles the menu, the cooking, the service and the cleanup, so you stand by the fire as a host, not a cook. Tell us your date, your headcount and your venue, and during our published business hours you'll have an itemised proposal promptly.

new_paragraphs: How much does BBQ catering cost in Dubai?

From AED 150 per person for a drop-off or buffet grill spread, with a minimum of 10 guests, 20 for a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900. A staffed live grill with a chef working the coals starts at AED 700 per person; premium proteins and plated service sit higher.
What is included in a BBQ catering package?

Included are menu design, a vetted private chef and grill team, all proteins and sides, the live cooking station, table or buffet service, and full setup and cleanup. Equipment, gas or charcoal and serviceware travel with the chef.
Is the BBQ food halal?

Yes, halal proteins are the standard, and the chef confirms sourcing on request. We also plan gluten-free, nut-free, dairy-free, vegetarian and vegan options into the menu from the start instead of as an afterthought.
Can you cater a BBQ at a villa, beach or rooftop?

Yes — villa gardens, pool decks, rooftops, beaches and desert sites are all workable. For beach and desert events we plan generator power, wind cover and safe fire management; compact electric grills cover apartments where an open flame is not allowed.
How many guests can you cater for?

The grill scales from an intimate dinner for a handful of guests to large parties and corporate events of 200 or more. Staffing and the number of grill stations are matched to your headcount and timing.
How far in advance should I book?

About 72 hours for a standard BBQ package, 3 to 5 days once a live grill station or multiple staff are involved, and 7 to 14 days for a wedding or a large corporate function. Short-notice requests are assessed individually against partner availability.
How do I hire BBQ catering near me in Dubai?
Send your date, guest count and venue through our enquiry form or WhatsApp, and we reply with an itemised proposal. A coordinator then confirms the menu, timings and setup before your event.
For bbq catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .

add_block.new_heading: The full BBQ menu, course by course
new_paragraphs: Here is the working menu in the order a Dubai grill event is served: the cold table first, hot starters while the coals come up, then the grill split into four separate families, a centrepiece if the occasion earns one, and dessert. You shortlist from each section and the chef builds the final menu around what you pick — none of this is a fixed package you have to take whole. What separates the best BBQ catering in Dubai from a page that says “steaks, ribs and prawns” is precisely this: named dishes, named cuts, named sauces.
1. Cold mezze and salads
The opening table, set out before anyone sits down. A typical menu draws five to eight of these; a larger buffet runs twelve.
Dips: hummus · moutabal · baba ghanouj · muhammara · labneh with garlic · shanklish (cheese with thyme)
Levantine salads: tabbouleh · fattoush · rocca with onion and tomato · rocca with feta · vine leaves (warak enab) · hindbeh (chicory in olive oil)
Grain salads: quinoa tabouleh · lentil tabouleh · kale and quinoa · freekeh salad
Western salads: Caesar with chicken · Greek salad · caprese · beetroot salad · beetroot boutabal · three bean salad · pasta salad · potato salad · green apple coleslaw · crab salad
On the table regardless: mixed olives and pickles · pickled cucumber · a fresh vegetable platter
2. Hot starters and pastries
These go out while the coals come up to temperature, so guests are eating within minutes of arriving instead of watching a cold grill.
Pastries: cheese sambousek · meat sambousek · spinach fatayer · cheese rolls · mousakhan rolls · mini lahem beajine, Trabolsi or Baalbaki style
Fried and spiced: fried kebbe (meat kibbeh) · falafel · potato with coriander · fried chicken liver · chicken wings · fried calamari · shrimps provencal · kofta balls with pomegranate
Sausage: makanek (Lebanese sausage) · sujouk
Fatteh: hummus fatteh · eggplant fatteh · shrimp fatteh
From the grill, early: arayes kafta — flatbread stuffed with spiced minced lamb and grilled until the outside crisps
3. The grill — Arabic mashawi
The core of a Dubai barbecue and the section most menus lead with. Most events run three to five of these; a full mixed grill covers the range in one platter.
Chicken: shish tawouk · chicken kafta · whole boneless chicken, butterflied and grilled flat
Lamb and beef: lamb kabab · kabab khoush khash · kabab orfali · lamb chops · lamb meat cubes · lamb loin · lahem meshwi (grilled meat)
Platters: mixed grill · mixed grill with tawouk · full mixed grill · mixed grill of meat
Alongside: makanek · sujouk · masbaha with pine nuts · grilled tomato and onion straight off the coals
4. The grill — Desi and subcontinental

Pakistani, North Indian and Afghani grilling, which is a different fire and a different marinade to the Levantine section above. Subcontinental hosts usually brief by ratio — two vegetarian to three non-vegetarian mains, for example — and the menu is built that way. The tandoor itself travels to villa gardens, driveways and permitted outdoor events, always outdoors and at ground level; it does not go into a villa kitchen, onto an apartment balcony or aboard a yacht. Where it cannot come, the naan, roti and tikka are fired in the licensed kitchen and finished hot at the station, so the bread still arrives blistered.
Kebabs: chicken seekh kebab · beef seekh kebab · chapli kebab
Tikka and boti: chicken tikka · tikka boti · malai boti (malai tikka) · fish tikka · paneer tikka · mutton ribs
From the tandoor: tandoori vegetables · naan and roti cooked to order
Curry and rice to go with it: chicken karahi · mutton biryani
5. The grill — continental and steakhouse cuts
This is usually what separates a premium menu from a standard one. Cut and provenance are stated, not implied.
Steaks: ribeye · picanha · Argentinian ribeye · wagyu skirt steak · Black Onyx tomahawk · tomahawk with rosemary and thyme gremolata, truffle butter, roast baby potatoes and vegetables
Slow beef: Angus short rib · wagyu beef cheeks
Chicken: grilled chicken · spiced chicken legs · honey-glazed chicken wings
Sausage: schubling · cheese knacker · beef chorizo
Sliders: beef slider · chicken slider · brisket sliders on soft potato buns with truffle aioli, caramelised onions, pickles and parmesan
6. Grilled seafood
Usually the upgrade that moves a menu to its top tier, and the section that carries a beach or yacht event.
Shellfish: grilled jumbo shrimp · tiger prawn skewers · lobster, 700–900g, split and grilled · lobster tail tacos · octopus provencal · fried calamari
Fish: grilled hammour fillet · BBQ hammour · salmon fillet · salmon skewers · smoked ocean trout · smoked salmon · herb-marinated fish
Larger dishes: fish sayadieh · seafood paella · mixed seafood skewers
7. The vegetarian and vegan grill
A section, not a footnote. Everything below is cooked on the grill in its own right, not assembled as a side.
Cheese and protein: grilled halloumi · paneer tikka · vegetarian burgers · falafel
Skewers: vegetable skewers · zucchini and eggplant · asparagus and artichoke · shiitake mushroom · negima (spring onion)
Whole vegetables: BBQ corn cob · grilled peppers · marinated mushrooms · grilled mixed vegetables · tandoori vegetables · sauteed vegetables
8. Smokehouse — low and slow

A separate register to the mashawi grill: hours of smoke instead of minutes of flame, sold by the kilo or as a feast board, not per skewer. Pork does not appear on it — where an American smokehouse would run pulled pork, this one runs pulled lamb. A live smoker is an outdoor, private-plot machine: villa garden, driveway, or a permitted event with the fire laid out clear of any marquee. It is not something an apartment tower will take, and it does not go on a boat. For those the same cuts are smoked in the licensed kitchen the day before, held hot and carved live on site — the carve is the part guests gather round, and it survives intact.
Beef: prime brisket · salt-and-pepper brisket · smoked wagyu brisket · wagyu smoked beef ribs · beef ribs · pastrami · beef chorizo
Lamb, chicken and duck: pulled lamb · smoked lamb leg · smoked whole chicken · smoked duck
Smokehouse sides: mandi rice · signature rice · coleslaw · potato salad · three bean salad · soft potato buns for building your own
9. Robata — Japanese charcoal skewers

The theatre tier: a charcoal counter where skewers are grilled to order and handed straight across. Sold by the skewer, so you decide how much of the menu each guest gets. The charcoal counter itself sets up in a villa garden or at a permitted outdoor event, standing clear of any tent fabric. In an apartment it runs on an electric yakitori grill instead — same skewers, same tare, same counter service, no charcoal aroma. On a yacht the boat's own fitted grill does the fire with the crew on it and a myCHEF chef skewering, glazing and plating alongside, which is how charter kitchens work anyway.
Chicken: chicken yakitori · teba (chicken wing) · tsukune (chicken balls) · negima (chicken and spring onion)
Seafood: scallop · shrimp · salmon · tsukune shrimp (prawn balls)
Beef: beef yakitori · short rib · wagyu skirt steak · beef and asparagus · enoki and short rib · asparagus and short rib
Vegetable: zucchini and eggplant · asparagus and artichoke · shiitake mushroom · tomato and white asparagus
10. The centrepiece and carvery station

One dish that gives the evening a photograph and a moment. A whole roast lamb is normally sized for a group of around thirty; smaller gatherings take a leg or a half. The carvery is also the one station that goes anywhere in Dubai — villa dining room, open public beach, apartment, terrace, yacht deck — because there is no flame, no fuel and no extraction question to answer, only hot-holding and a carving lamp. That is why it carries the menu at the venues where the fired stations cannot come.
Whole lamb: whole lamb spit roast · whole lamb, oriental, biryani or friki style · half lamb, same three styles · a lamb roasting station built on a 13kg Australian lamb
Lamb dishes carved to order: lamb ouzi · mansaf kharouf · mutton ra’an · roasted baby leg of lamb · lamb leg, oriental, biryani or friki
Beef and poultry: slow-roasted beef ribeye carved to order · whole turkey with oriental rice
11. Rice, staples and hot sides
A rice is non-negotiable on any Arabic or Desi grill menu. Two to five of these usually go out.
Rice: white basmati · Arabic rice · biryani rice · chicken biryani · chicken kabseh · lamb kabseh · chicken freekeh · moghrabieh with meat and chicken
Potato: roasted potatoes · country potato · batata fries · Cajun sweet-potato oven fries · baked potatoes with sauerkraut and creme fraiche
Vegetable sides: fasolia bil zeit · bamieh bil zeit · collard greens and green beans · cassoulet spiced mixed beans · herbed couscous · grilled tomato and onion
12. Breads and the saj station

The saj is the easiest live station to place: a small domed griddle, low flame, no embers. A gas saj works at a villa outdoors and at permitted outdoor events; an electric saj carries no fuel question at all, which is the version specified for apartments and terraces. On a yacht it does not run, because no catering gas cylinder may be brought aboard — there the breads are baked in the licensed kitchen and filled and rolled to order on deck, which keeps the live element and loses only the griddle.
Standard: fresh Arabic bread · fresh-baked pita · kaak bread · potato buns for the sliders · naan from the tandoor
Live saj station: zaatar · cheese · kishek · lahem beajine, rolled and griddled in front of guests
Live Arabic bread oven: manakeesh in zaatar, cheese, meat, turkey and cheese, or Nutella
13. Sauces, relishes and dips
Named individually, because “assorted sauces” tells you nothing. Four to six travel with the grill.
Arabic: garlic toum · hummus as an accompaniment · yoghurt with cucumber and mint
BBQ and smoke: peach habanero BBQ sauce · marmalade smoked tonkatsu BBQ sauce · creamy BBQ · mustard
Relish and herb: house-made tomato relish · beetroot relish · maple syrup, chilli, pineapple and vanilla relish · gremolata · chimichurri
14. Dessert
Arabic: cheese kunafa · halawet el jibben · othmalieh, cheese or kashta · umm ali · znood el sit · mafroukeh · maamoul bil ashta · mixed baklawa · mohalabieh · halawet el riz · katayef kashta
Western: creme caramel · cheesecake · tiramisu · black forest · assorted mini cakes · macarons
Fruit: fresh fruit salad · sliced fruit platter
Live stations you can run alongside the grill

Each of these is a second cooking point with its own setup and its own queue, and each is priced as an addition instead of being folded into the per-head rate: a shawarma spit, a saj bread station, a falafel station, a burger station, a fajita station, a pasta station, a rotisserie chicken station, a tandoor, a carvery station and a live dessert station. Two stations is the usual limit before an event starts to feel like a food hall instead of a dinner. The shawarma spit is the one worth settling early: gas-fired, tall and heavy, it belongs at a villa or a permitted outdoor event, and it is not something a yacht will take. Where it cannot come the cone is cooked in the licensed kitchen, carried hot on its skewer and shaved to order at a carving station — guests watch the same ritual, and the fire simply happened two hours earlier.

add_block.new_heading: Halal, vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free on the grill
new_paragraphs: Halal is the standard on every menu above, not an option you have to ask for, and pork appears nowhere on the list. Culinary preparation is performed by licensed culinary partners, each holding the trade licences and food-safety approvals applicable to the specific services it performs, and we will walk you through what documentation the kitchen serving your event can produce.

Vegetarian is section seven, not a single skewer added at the end — halloumi, paneer tikka, corn cob and four kinds of vegetable skewer will feed a vegetarian guest properly. Vegan works from the same section with the cheese dropped: the skewers, corn, mushrooms, peppers, falafel and most of the cold mezze are already plant-based, and the chef confirms which dips were made with yoghurt.

Gluten-free is where the Dubai market is weakest — most grill menus name it and then go quiet on which dishes qualify. Dish by dish: the grilled and smoked meats, the fish, the vegetable skewers and the rice dishes are fine; the risk sits in the breads, the kibbeh, the sambousek, the couscous and the fatteh, which are all built on wheat. Ask and you get that list applied to your specific menu before you sign it off, and the chef confirms sourcing and cross-contact handling.

add_block.new_heading: Indoor BBQ, outdoor BBQ, and the cheaper formats
new_paragraphs: Not every event has a garden, and the venue decides the fire more than the menu does. Dubai Municipality is blunt about the indoor case in its own barbecue guidance — do not light coal in an enclosed space or indoors — so for indoor BBQ catering in a villa, a majlis or an office floor the cooking moves to compact electric grills, a plancha or an electric tandoor, with the long smoking done before service and the finishing done in front of guests. In an apartment tower the line is firmer and it is written down: Emaar's vertical-community rules prohibit barbecues, grills or cooking equipment of any kind on balconies and terraces whatever the fuel, and no LPG cylinder may be brought into the tower or the unit. An apartment grill is therefore induction and plancha, with everything fired coming hot from the licensed kitchen. On a rooftop or at a desert camp there is no published rule to quote either way, so myCHEF confirms the setup with the building management or the site operator before quoting rather than discovering it on the night. Where flame is limited, gas or electric covers the same dish list with a shorter char.

On budget: nobody should pretend a staffed live grill is cheap BBQ catering. If cost is the deciding factor, the volume formats put the same food on the table without a chef stationed at your venue — a drop-off grill spread in portioned boxes, or a self-service buffet with chafing dishes — from AED 150 per person, with a minimum of 10 guests, 20 for a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900. A staffed live grill, where a chef works the coals in front of your guests and serves through the evening, starts at AED 700 per person. The difference between those two numbers is service and theatre, not the quality of the meat.

add_block.new_heading: If you were searching for a BBQ restaurant instead
new_paragraphs: A lot of people who land here started out looking for a BBQ restaurant in Dubai — a grill house in Dubai Mall, a terrace table in Dubai Marina — and stopped because the table was too small, the booking was gone, or the group could not be seated together. Catering answers a different problem: the grill travels to your venue, you set the headcount, and nobody is timing your table. One honest limit worth stating: Korean BBQ, where guests cook at their own table-top grill, is a restaurant format built around fixed equipment at every seat, and it is not something arranged for private homes. The nearest live-fire equivalent on this menu is the robata counter in section nine, where a chef grills skewers to order and hands them straight across.

new_paragraphs: Your venue shapes the setup, and we plan it around the space you have. A villa garden, a rooftop terrace, a pool deck or a beach spot each has different access, power and ventilation needs, and the chef assesses them before the date so the grill sits safely and the smoke drains away from guests. We bring the grills, gas or charcoal, prep tables, serviceware and staff; you provide the space and, where needed, permission from the community or venue. On a Dubai beach the answer turns on which of four situations you are in: on an open public beach, lighting a fire outside a designated zone is a Dubai Municipality offence carrying a Dh500 fine, so the menu runs on carvery and an electric plancha line; in a Municipality beach park charcoal is limited to the fixed BBQ stations; at a permitted private event on the sand, or at a beach club with its own approved cooking line, the full grill runs. For beach and desert settings we plan generator power, wind cover and safe fire management on top of that. This kind of BBQ home catering works in apartments too, using compact electric grills where an open flame is not allowed. Setup, service and a full clear-down are all included, so the venue is handed back exactly as we found it.

add_block.new_heading: How much does BBQ catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: BBQ catering cost in Dubai splits at the service line. A drop-off grill spread or a self-service buffet starts at AED 150 per person, with a 10-guest minimum, 20 for a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900. A staffed live grill, where a chef works the coals through the evening and serves your guests, starts at AED 700 per person and a plated version with premium proteins sits higher again. Set BBQ catering packages are available at fixed per-head rates, which keeps budgeting predictable for larger parties, while bespoke menus are quoted line by line. There's no single sticker price, because a beach event with generators is a different job from a villa garden dinner — but the quote is typically itemised, so you can see where every dirham goes and trim or add to fit your budget. For a full breakdown of BBQ catering prices and what drives them, see our Dubai catering price guide , or send your details for an exact figure. Whether you want an affordable family grill or a luxury seafood-led feast, the price tracks the choices you make.

Second, we send an itemised proposal — usually within one business day, often promptly during our published business hours — with the menu, the staffing and the all-in cost. Third, we confirm the details: dietary needs, timings, grill placement and any venue permissions. Fourth, on the day the chef and team arrive, set up, cook and clear down. Searching for BBQ catering near me shouldn't mean chasing quotes for a week — one message gets you a real menu and a real number. To hire BBQ catering for your event, start with our enquiry form or WhatsApp , and a coordinator picks it up from there.

add_block.new_heading: Why book BBQ catering with myCHEF?
new_paragraphs: MyCHEF was founded by a chef trained in some of Europe's most demanding kitchens, on one idea: you own the evening, we carry the work. No chef is offered for bbq catering before clearing identity checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing performance reviews — a continuous standard, not a one-time tick. We are honest about it, too: no system removes every risk, so we match each event to the chef well suited to it.

For a live-fire occasion like this, that might be Ahmed Al-Rashid — 18+ years across Dubai, London and Paris in classical French technique — who designs each menu as a collaboration with the host, every course timed, seasoned and served to exacting standards. We have run bbq catering alongside villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas across Dubai. Client reviews are added as events run.
